methods.name: Seismicity lineament detection (H50-B)
methods.citation: Ouillon, Ducorbier & Sornette (2008), Tectonophysics 456, 42; Ouillon & Sornette (2011), J. Geophys. Res. 116, B01303
methods.used: Legacy H50-B corridor orientation via 2-D inertia tensor and Poisson nearest-neighbour crossover. The 2-D triangle-area analogue of the 3-D tetrahedron statistic is an unverified project adaptation; the builder computes its keep mask but does not apply it to subsequent lineation inputs. This is not demonstrated effective declustering.

methods.name: Marginal-credit emission
methods.used: a dot is emitted iff its kernel credit k exceeds 0.2*s; binary support dominates any graded map

caveats: The private leaderboard is unknown to this project; no number here is a leaderboard score.

Legacy H50-B local equal-budget comparisons did not consistently beat smoothed density on both proxy frames; its prior artifact retained a low-weight component, which is not a current recommendation or an H50-S1 holdout result.
Component 0.2778 attribution is owner-reported, not organizer-confirmed (GEMSDOE32/docs/research/why-d28-scored-026.md).

ComCat public access does not settle contributor-specific rights for the mixed-network export; do not label the extract US public domain or use it as an external competition input without source-specific review.
Legacy H50-B local density comparisons are not the frozen H50-S1 four-macrofold evaluation, and the legacy method is not a current official score or a score-to-TIFF mapping.
H51 emits nothing within 300 m of the provided catalogue by design, so the given-catalogue raster is an anti-instrument for H51 and its score there is not evidence about the method.

The H51 mass selection rests on a single measured SGMC-off-to-hidden transfer factor (0.28, from one owner file with both a live and a local score); the full per-mass table is published so the mass can be moved with one argument.
